title: Finite Tor intervals and bounded flat models on a ringed site
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the chosen universe [def-weil-size-convention], and let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Use the abelian category of sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], its unbounded derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], and derived tensor computed by K-flat resolutions [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Let $K\in D(R)$ and $a\leq b$ be integers. The following conditions are equivalent:

(1) For every sheaf $M$ of $R$-modules placed in degree zero, $H^i(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M)=0$ whenever $i\notin[a,b]$.

(2) There is a cochain complex $P$ of $R$-module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], with every $P^i$ flat (tensoring with it is exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]), $P^i=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$, and an isomorphism $K\simeq P$ in $D(R)$.

No constructibility hypothesis, existence of enough points, or constant-coefficient assumption is imposed.

proof.text:
We first make the single-variable tensor computation explicit. Let $T$ be a K-flat complex with flat terms and let $M$ be a module sheaf. Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $c:C\to M[0]$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The cone of $c$ is acyclic by [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic]. By [lem-pc-tensor-mapping-cone-iso] the cone of $T\otimes c$ is $\operatorname{Tot}(T\otimes\operatorname{Cone}(c))$, which is acyclic by [def-pc-kflat-complex]; the symmetry from [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] exchanges the factors in that definition (on complexes it has sign $(-1)^{pq}$). Thus $T\otimes c$ is a quasi-isomorphism by the same cone criterion. The two-K-flat computation in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] now gives
$$Q_RT\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M\simeq Q_R\operatorname{Tot}(T\otimes_R M[0]).$$
This is the direct cone criterion applied to the chosen resolution, not an assumption that $M[0]$ is K-flat.

source.place: Tags 06YP (lemma-K-flat-quasi-isomorphism) and 06YU (definition-derived-tor); the cone argument in the proof of 06YP

proof.text: Assume (2). The displayed $P$ is bounded above and termwise flat, so [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] makes it K-flat. Apply step 1 with $T=P$. In degree $i$ the tensor with $M[0]$ has just the term $P^i\otimes_R M$, by [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and is zero outside $[a,b]$. Its cohomology is therefore zero outside that interval. The isomorphism $K\simeq Q_RP$ and functoriality of derived tensor give (1).

Assume (1) and test it on $M=R$. The ordinary tensor unit is $R$, by [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], so it is flat: tensoring with it is the identity exact functor [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. For a flat-term K-flat representative $T$ of $K$, provided by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], step 1 and the termwise unit isomorphisms identify $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R$ with $K$. Hence $H^i(K)=0$ outside $[a,b]$. By the representative characterization in [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], choose a complex $L$ representing $K$ with $L^i=0$ for $i>b$. This uses only the upper bound on cohomology; it makes no assertion that the terms of $L$ are flat.

source.place: Tag 08G1, proof of (1) implies (2), first paragraph; preceding observation testing on the ring sheaf

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement] to the complex $L$ of step 3 with the integer $N=b$. Obtain a quasi-isomorphism $F\to L$ with every $F^i$ flat and $F^i=0$ for $i>b$. Thus $Q_RF\simeq K$, since the derived category inverts quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The bound is exactly $b$, not merely some larger integer. This replaces the finite sequence of upper flat-kernel truncations in the source proof by the already available bound-preserving flat replacement.

proof.text:
The bounded-above flat complex $F$ is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. Step 1 therefore identifies $H^{a-1}(F\otimes_R M[0])$ with $H^{a-1}(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M)$ for every module sheaf $M$. This vanishes by (1), because $a-1<a$. Symmetry of the sheaf tensor [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] interchanges $F\otimes M[0]$ and $M[0]\otimes F$; the degree-zero factor contributes no sign. All the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-site-flat-opcycles-tor-criterion] hold with $P=F$ and $n=a$. It follows that the cokernel sheaf
$$B=\operatorname{Coker}(d_F^{a-1}:F^{a-1}\to F^a)$$
is flat. In particular, it is exactness after tensoring with every module sheaf, not flatness of the cohomology sheaves of $K$, that supplies the bottom flat term.

Define $P$ explicitly by $P^i=0$ for $i<a$, $P^a=B$, and $P^i=F^i$ for $i>a$. The differential out of $B$ is induced by $d_F^a$, which kills $\operatorname{im}d_F^{a-1}$ because $d_F^ad_F^{a-1}=0$; subsequent differentials are those of $F$. This is a complex by [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. The quotient in degree $a$ and the identity in higher degrees define a chain map $q:F\to P$. Using the cohomology quotient formula in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], in degree $a$ its induced map is
$$\ker d_F^a/\operatorname{im}d_F^{a-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}\ker(B\to F^{a+1}).$$
In degree $a+1$, the images of $B\to F^{a+1}$ and $F^a\to F^{a+1}$ coincide since $F^a\to B$ is epimorphic; thus cohomology is unchanged there, and it is unchanged in every higher degree. Below $a$ both cohomologies vanish, for $F$ by step 3 and for $P$ by its zero terms. Hence $q$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $Q_RP\simeq Q_RF\simeq K$. The bottom term is flat by step 5, higher terms are flat by step 4, and zero terms are flat since tensoring with zero is the zero exact functor [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Finally $a\leq b$ and $F^i=0$ for $i>b$ imply $P^i=0$ outside $[a,b]$. This is (2).
